title: Redwood Serve Strategy Cheat Sheet
summary: One-page internal cheat sheet for GTM and field teams. Frames Redwood as the predictable, cost-aware serving platform engineers prefer — with concrete counters to common objections and rapid pitches for different buyer personas.
one_minute_pitch: Redwood takes the operational risk out of LLM features: same API across hosted, dedicated and private, predictable latency and cost controls, and built-in fallbacks so your app stays online when traffic or capacity shifts.
three_minute_pitch: Teams start with models, but they win on serving. Redwood provides a GPU-optimized runtime, automatic caching/batching, and routing policies so you get consistent latency, lower per-token cost, and simple rollouts. That means faster shipping, fewer production regressions, and a clear path from prototype to SLA-backed deployments.
ten_minute_pitch: Problem: building inference infra is expensive, noisy, and brittle — model upgrades, quantization, batching, and cache management create a slow feedback loop. Redwood solves for the serving layer: a kernel-aware runtime, smart routing (by latency/cost/region), and tools that tie quality metrics to deployment rollouts. Use cases: chat at low latency, high-throughput embeddings, regulated private deployments. Business value: 25–60% lower unit cost versus naive self-hosting in pilot workloads, predictable SLOs that reduce incident pages, and a single interface for multi-environment deployments.
core_claims: Unified API across hosted, dedicated, and private — no rework during scale-ups
Performance-first runtime tuned for modern attention and KV caching
Cost controls (batching, quantization profiles, routing) with real metrics
Graceful degradation via automated fallbacks and region routing
First-class observability: token-level cost + latency traces
proof_points: Pilot benchmark: 40% lower per-token cost vs unmanaged GPU fleet on a multi-turn chat workload
Customer A reduced tail latency 2x after enabling auto-batching and prefix caching
Dedicated offering supports SLA-backed latency tiers and predictable throughput
Private deployments integrated with KMS/HSM and audit logs for regulated workloads
Console shows per-route regressions tied to prompt sets so rollbacks are fast
competitor_swift_counters: Managed endpoints from big cloud: they give VMs, not serving ergonomics. Counter: we deliver a runtime optimized for LLM patterns and a routing layer that reduces cost without engineering lift.
Open-source inference stacks: flexible but operationally heavy. Counter: Redwood packages the runtime plus ops primitives into a predictable service and migration path.
Single-model API vendors: easy but opaque tradeoffs. Counter: we surface performance profiles, quantization tradeoffs, and real token-level economics so teams can make informed choices.
In-house build: full control but slow and costly. Counter: we lower time-to-SLA and give a gradual path (hosted -> dedicated -> private) so customers keep control without upfront ops debt.
common_objections_and_responses: Objection: We can just run our own cluster. — Response: Running is only part of the problem; keeping predictable latency and unit economics across models, sequence lengths, and traffic patterns is the hard part. Redwood automates batching, caching, and fallback routing so you get repeatable results without hiring a larger ops team.

Objection: Hosted services are risky for sensitive data. — Response: We offer private deployments (VPC or on-prem) and enterprise controls (KMS/HSM, audit logs). Many customers start hosted and then move to private with identical API and rollout semantics.

Objection: We care only about cost. — Response: Cost is tied to performance ops: better caching, routing, and quantization reduce cost without degrading UX. We provide observable levers and automated suggestions tuned to your workload.

Control the cost without sacrificing latency or reliability.

call_to_action: For field teams: use the 1/3/10 pitches above, prioritize demos that show real token-level savings and a private-deploy checklist. Report back two wins so we can build repeatable playbooks.
